To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elderly patients hospitalized for psychiatric disorders have a high prevalence of comorbid physical illness and complex care needs immediately following hospital discharge, but there are few studies specifically examining transitional care needs for this population.

elderly patients discharged from a psychiatric hospital are at risk of poor outcomes due to complex medical and psychiatric care needs and that transitional care interventions targeting elderly patients discharged from the medical hospital may be effective in improving the care transitions of elderly patients discharged from psychiatry.
elderly depressed patients have complex needs that are poorly met by the current health care system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of treatment for patients who are in need of care.

the development of a new model of transitional care for depressed elderly patients, and with the evaluation of the effectiveness of this model in terms of the quality of care, and of its impact on costs and on the patients' quality of life.
the development and evaluation of an intervention that aims to improve the quality and safety of care for elderly patients discharged after hospitalization for depression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transitional care needs are not being met for severely depressed elderly patients.
the transitional care needs for elderly patients with major depression have been poorly addressed and there is a lack of evidence-based interventions to address this problem.

there is a lack of literature specifically addressing the needs and barriers to care of severely depressed elderly patients in the immediate post-hospitalization period, and that there is a need to develop and evaluate transitional care interventions for this population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to do a better job in the care of elderly patients with depression, particularly those who are medically ill.
the elderly are at risk for poor transitional care after discharge from a medical hospital.
there is no research that specifically addresses the post-hospitalization care needs of severely depressed elderly patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the care of elderly patients with depression is a complex, multidisciplinary, and interdisciplinary process.
the care transitions of severely depressed elderly patients need to be improved to prevent rehospitalization, and to promote better health and quality of life.
the transitional care needs are complex, and require a comprehensive and multidisciplinary approach.
